author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Lindsay Clancy’s defense attorney has asked a Plymouth Superior Court judge to enter a required finding of not guilty after the recent jury deadlock ended her trial in a mistrial.

WHDH reported that attorney Kevin Reddington filed the six-page motion Thursday. The request argues that prosecutors did not present enough evidence for a juror seeking the truth to find guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.

The filing also challenges whether the state proved that Clancy was mentally capable of conforming her conduct to the law. That issue was central to the case and to the jury’s inability to reach a unanimous verdict. The motion asks Judge William Sullivan to resolve the case rather than send it toward another trial.

A filing is a request, not a ruling, and the court has not yet granted the defense’s motion. The next significant step will be the judge’s response after the prosecution has an opportunity to address the arguments. Until then, the mistrial remains the case’s latest completed proceeding and the criminal charges have not been dismissed.
dek: Attorney Kevin Reddington filed a six-page motion asking the judge to enter a required finding of not guilty after jurors deadlocked.
headline: Lindsay Clancy’s defense seeks not-guilty finding after mistrial
